# Write to a repository without a clone

## Intent

An agent or a developer can change a workspace's repository with plain HTTP requests and no working copy: commit a set of file edits in one request, create, move and delete branches and tags, and rebase a branch on the server. Every such write is guarded by a compare-and-swap, so nobody overwrites work they have not seen, and it obeys the same push rules and has the same consequences as a git push, so the REST API and the git server stay two doors to one repository.

## Goals

- `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` builds one commit from up to 1,000 file operations and moves one branch, or creates it, in one request.
- A write against a head the caller has not seen answers `409 ref_moved` with the current head and changes nothing.
- `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/workspaces/:slug/scm/refs` create, move and delete branches and tags.
- `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/rebase` replays a branch onto another revision and answers a conflict report when it cannot.
- Every write is refused by the push rules exactly where a git push of the same update would be, with `403` and one `error_type` per rule.
- The workspace's owner and the admin token can move a protected branch forward through the API as a direct push.
- Every accepted write emits `parley.git.push` with `via: "api"`; a commit also emits `parley.scm.commit`.
- `parley scm commit` and `parley scm rebase` drive the two calls from a shell.

## Non-goals

- The read routes and read commands of the source control API, the ref and commit objects, and `[scm].max_file_size` and `[scm].read_timeout`: package 20 scm_read_api.
- The push rules themselves (which update each rule refuses, the owner exemption's four conditions, the path check of a path-scoped token), the `parley.git.push` event's definition and the update of the workspace's `head_sha`: package 18 git_push_rules. This package calls that rule engine (`Evaluate`) and that ref writer (`Apply` with `via: "api"`) in `internal/gitserver/pushrule`, reports the verdict, and has no ref writer of its own.
- Carry-patch push control (integration and patch branches, forwarding to origin): package 37 carry_patch_push_control, reached through the rule engine.
- Opening a change, recording a version and the validation of CHG-FR-003: package 22 change_opening_and_versions. This package declares the interface `ChangeLinker` in `internal/scm/linker.go` (find the open change of a branch, check an opening, open a change) and package 22 registers its implementation. Versions are recorded by the ref-updated stage package 22 registers with the ref writer of package 18; this package only names the version kind (`commit`, `ref`, `rebase`).
- The mapping of a git push to a change and the `parley.*` push options: package 19 git_push_to_change.
- The session-linking rule: package 49 agent_sessions_and_usage, called through the interface `SessionLinker` declared in `internal/scm/session.go`.
- The full conflict report (the `landed_changes` and `landed_by` attribution) and the conflict routes: package 26 conflict_reports_and_resolution. The report type itself is `ConflictReport` of `internal/gitrepo`, declared by package 20.
- Recording a fork's last activity: the ref writer of package 18 reports every accepted API write on a fork to the recorder of package 16; this package makes no call of its own.
- Restack of dependent changes after a new version: package 24 change_stacks_and_restack.
- The error envelope, check order, body rules and `Idempotency-Key` mechanics: package 02 http_api_conventions. The CLI's settings, output and exit codes: package 09 cli_foundation.
- CLI commands for ref create, move and delete: the PRD keeps those REST only.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. The source control API is §6 of the product PRD (`docs/prd/06_source_control_api.md`). Package 20 delivers its read half in `internal/scm` and the git wrapper in `internal/gitrepo`; package 18 delivers the push rule engine and the ref writer in `internal/gitserver/pushrule`. This package adds the write half: the handlers in `internal/scm`, the tree-building and rebase operations they need in `internal/gitrepo`, the `[scm].max_commit_size` key in `internal/config`, and two commands in `internal/cli/scm.go`.

Callers are agents (a PAT, often bound to a task fork and limited to paths), developers (an API key), review and revert tooling, and the operator (the admin token). All routes are under `/api/v1/workspaces/:slug/scm`.

## Requirements

### Who may write, and when (SCM-FR-020)

Every write route needs the scope `git:write` when the credential is a PAT (`403 insufficient_scope` otherwise) and write access to the workspace (`404 not_found` for a caller with no access, `403 forbidden` for a caller with read access only). After that the workspace's status decides: `archived` answers `409 workspace_archived`; a fork whose parent is archived answers `409 parent_archived`; `pending`, `cloning` or a running reclone, archive or delete answers `409 workspace_busy`; `failed` answers `409 workspace_not_ready`. A refused request writes nothing and emits nothing. The five write routes are `POST …/scm/commits`, `POST …/scm/refs`, `PATCH …/scm/refs/*name`, `DELETE …/scm/refs/*name` and `POST …/scm/rebase`.

### Commit creation (SCM-FR-022)

`POST …/scm/commits` takes `branch`, `message`, `operations`, and optionally `expected_head_sha`, `base_ref`, `author {name, email}`, `allow_empty`, `session_id` and `change`. The body may be up to `[scm].max_commit_size` (default 32 MiB); a larger body answers `413 payload_too_large`. At most 1,000 operations are accepted.

1. The parent. If the branch exists, the parent is its head and `expected_head_sha` must equal it; a different or absent value answers `409 ref_moved` with `details.current_sha`. `base_ref` is ignored for an existing branch. If the branch does not exist, `base_ref` is required (`400 invalid_request` without it) and the parent is the commit it resolves to (`404 ref_not_found` when it resolves to nothing).
2. The operations are applied in order to the parent's tree (next area).
3. A commit whose tree equals its parent's tree answers `400 empty_commit`, unless `allow_empty` is true.
4. The commit has the given message, the given author or else the caller's name and e-mail, and the hub as committer.
5. The branch moves from the parent to the new commit by compare-and-swap. A lost race answers `409 ref_moved` and leaves nothing visible: no ref moved, no event, no change touched.

The answer is `201 {commit, branch, change, change_error}` with the commit object and ref object of package 20.

### File operations (§6.3, §6.9)

| `op` | Fields | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `put` | `path`; `content` (UTF-8) or `content_base64`; optional `mode` (`100644` default, `100755`, `120000`) | create or replace the file |
| `delete` | `path` | remove the file; it must exist |
| `move` | `from`, `to` | rename; `from` must exist and `to` must not |
| `chmod` | `path`, `mode` | change the mode only |

A path is repository-relative with `/` separators and must not be empty, start with `/`, contain a `.` or `..` segment, or name anything under `.git`. A malformed operation (unknown `op`, a bad path, both or neither of `content` and `content_base64`, a mode outside the three) answers `400 invalid_request`. An operation that is well formed and cannot apply to the tree as it stands answers `400 invalid_operation` and names the operation's zero-based index: deleting, moving or changing the mode of a missing path; moving onto an existing path; a `put` under a path that is a file; a `put` onto a directory; any write to a submodule entry. Two operations on one path apply in order, so `put a` then `delete a` leaves no `a`. A `put` whose content equals the file is allowed; only a commit that changes nothing is empty. Symlink content is the link target as text.

### Consequences of a commit (SCM-FR-023, SCM-FR-024, SCM-FR-027)

A successful commit has the consequences of a push of that commit: `parley.git.push` (`via: "api"`) and `parley.scm.commit` (`branch`, `sha`, `parent_sha`, `files`: the paths touched, at most 100) are emitted; a version of kind `commit` is recorded, in the transaction of the ref update, when the branch is the source of a `draft` or `open` change; a change is opened when the request carries a `change` object, or when the workspace is a fork with `auto_change` on and the branch has no `draft` or `open` change. With an explicit `change` object, a failed check (`403 insufficient_scope` without `changes:write`, or the `400`/`409` of CHG-FR-003) refuses the whole request and nothing becomes visible. In an `auto_change` fork without a `change` object the commit is kept, `change` is `null` and `change_error {error_type, message}` says why.

`session_id`, on a commit or a rebase, must satisfy the session-linking rule of §14; otherwise `400 unknown_session` and nothing is written. It is recorded on the commit, the events and any version.

The three `POST` write routes take `Idempotency-Key`: a replay answers `200` with the first answer's body and creates nothing.

### Push rules over the API (SCM-FR-021)

Every write is checked by the rule engine of package 18 as the ref update it is. A refusal is `403` with the rule's message from GIT-FR-030 and this `error_type`:

| Rule | `error_type` |
|---|---|
| 1 hub-owned refs (`refs/parley/**`) | `hub_owned_ref` |
| 2 protected branches | `protected_branch` |
| 2a default branch deletion | `default_branch` |
| 3 tracking branches of a fork | `tracking_branch` (with `details.base_ref`, the fork's base branch) |
| 4 carry-patch, integration branch | `integration_branch` |
| 4 carry-patch, patch branch | `patch_branch` |
| 5 path-scoped token | `path_not_allowed` (with the offending `path`) |

A refused write moves no ref, emits no event and touches no change. A rule that cannot be evaluated answers `500 internal`; rules never fail open.

### Direct push through the API (SCM-FR-028)

The owner exemption of GIT-FR-034 applies as over git. A commit on a protected branch, a fast-forward ref move of one, and a rebase that leaves one a fast-forward of its old head pass for the workspace's owner and the admin token, with an API key, the admin token or a PAT that is neither workspace-bound nor path-scoped, while `protect.owner_push` is true. The `parley.git.push` event then has `direct: true`, and no change is opened and no version recorded for the branch. A `change` object in a commit request on a protected branch answers `400 invalid_request` before anything is written. A create, a backwards or sideways move and a delete of a protected branch are `403 protected_branch` for every caller.

### Refs (SCM-FR-025)

- `POST …/scm/refs` with `{name, sha | ref}` creates a branch or a tag and answers `201` with the ref object. A bare name is a branch. Exactly one of `sha`, `ref`. Errors: `400 invalid_request` (bad name, a namespace other than `refs/heads/`, `refs/tags/` or `refs/parley/`, both or neither target); `404 ref_not_found` (target resolves to no commit); `409 ref_exists`. Event: `parley.git.push` with `created: true`.
- `PATCH …/scm/refs/*name` with `{sha, expected_sha}` moves a ref by compare-and-swap and answers `200` with the ref object. Errors: `409 ref_moved` with `details.current_sha`; `404 ref_not_found`. A move that is not a fast-forward is allowed on an unprotected branch and reported with `forced: true`. A branch that is a change's source gets a version of kind `ref`.
- `DELETE …/scm/refs/*name` with optional `expected_sha` answers `204`. Errors: `409 ref_moved`; `409 ref_in_use` when the branch is the source of a `draft` or `open` change; `403 default_branch`; `404 ref_not_found`. Event: `parley.git.push` with `deleted: true`.

### Server-side rebase (SCM-FR-026)

`POST …/scm/rebase` with `{branch, onto, expected_head_sha?, session_id?}` replays the commits of `branch` that are not in `onto` on top of `onto` and moves `branch` by compare-and-swap. The answer is `200 {status, branch, old_head_sha, new_head_sha, onto_sha, change}`. A branch already based on `onto` answers `status: "up_to_date"` and nothing moves. A branch whose every commit is already in `onto` moves to `onto` and reports `rebased`. On conflict nothing changes and the answer is `409 rebase_conflict` with the conflict report in `details`. Merge commits in the range answer `400 merge_commits_unsupported`. A stale `expected_head_sha` or a lost race answers `409 ref_moved`. Rebasing the source branch of a change records a version of kind `rebase`.

### CLI (§6.6)

- `parley scm commit <slug>` with `--branch` (required), `--message` (required), `--base`, `--expected-head`, repeatable `--put <repo-path>=<local-file>`, `--delete <repo-path>` and `--move <from>=<to>`, `--session`, `--change-target`, `--title`, `--intent`, `--draft`. Without `--expected-head` it first reads the branch with `GET …/scm/refs/*name` and uses its head. It prints the hub's answer. `409 ref_moved` prints the envelope on stderr and exits 1; the command does not retry.
- `parley scm rebase <slug> <branch>` with `--onto` (required) and `--expected-head`. A conflict prints the envelope with the conflict report on stderr and exits 1.

### End-to-end flows

1. An agent with a fork-bound PAT posts a commit with three operations to a new branch of its fork, naming `base_ref`. The hub builds the commit, passes the push rules, creates the branch and emits both events. The agent reads the file back through the read API, then posts a second commit with the old head and receives `409 ref_moved` with the current head.
2. A developer runs `parley scm commit` to add a local file to a branch, another commit lands on the target branch, and the developer runs `parley scm rebase --onto`. The hub replays the commit and moves the branch; the command prints `status: "rebased"`.
3. The workspace's owner commits to the protected default branch with an API key and the commit is accepted as a direct push; the same request with the owner's workspace-bound PAT is refused with `403 protected_branch`, an org member's is refused with `403 forbidden`, and the branch does not move.

## Design Decisions

1. Project decisions relied on: Go; bare repositories on disk; git operations run the `git` binary through `internal/gitrepo` (no git library); `net/http` router; `github.com/spf13/cobra` for the CLI; tests use `testing`, `net/http/httptest` and repositories made with `git init` in `t.TempDir()`.
2. A commit's tree is built without a working tree: a temporary index file, `git read-tree`, `git hash-object -w`, `git update-index --cacheinfo`, `git write-tree`, `git commit-tree`. Objects written for a request that is then refused stay unreferenced; "nothing is written" means no ref moved, no event and no change touched.
3. Order of checks inside commit creation, after the route gate: body shape and operation shape (`400 invalid_request`), the `change` object on a protected branch (`400`), `session_id` (`400 unknown_session`), the parent (`409 ref_moved`, `404 ref_not_found`), the operations (`400 invalid_operation`), emptiness (`400 empty_commit`), the push rules (`403`), the explicit change check, the compare-and-swap. SCM-FR-022 fixes the middle of this order; the rest is the simplest order in which each check has its inputs.
4. An existing branch with no `expected_head_sha` answers `409 ref_moved` with the current head, the literal reading of SCM-FR-022 step 1, so a client can retry from one answer.
5. `operations` may be empty or absent; the commit is then empty and needs `allow_empty`.
6. `invalid_operation` names the index as `details.index`, zero-based. `tracking_branch` names the fork's base as `details.base_ref` (`fork_point.ref`). `path_not_allowed` carries `path` as a named member of `error`, as SCM-FR-021 says.
7. A ref name under `refs/parley/` is refused by rule 1 (`403 hub_owned_ref`); any other namespace outside `refs/heads/` and `refs/tags/` is `400 invalid_request`. This keeps both SCM-FR-021 and SCM-FR-025 true.
8. Tags written through the API are lightweight and can be moved and deleted with the same routes as branches. A ref's target must be a commit.
9. A `PATCH` whose `sha` equals the ref's current commit answers `200` and emits nothing, as a push with no change does (GIT-FR-025).
10. `Idempotency-Key` replays apply to the three `POST` routes, as PLAT-FR-015 defines. `PATCH` and `DELETE` accept the header and ignore it; `expected_sha` already makes them safe to retry.
11. Changes and sessions are reached through two interfaces declared in `internal/scm`, `ChangeLinker` (`linker.go`) and `SessionLinker` (`session.go`), because packages 22 and 49 are built after this one. Until package 22 registers its implementation, no branch is a change's source and a request with a `change` object answers `400 invalid_request`. Until package 49 registers its implementation, every `session_id` is refused with `unknown_session`: an unverifiable reference is never accepted. `SessionLinker` has the same name and check in `internal/gitserver` (package 19) and `internal/change` (package 22). Here and in package 19 it is check-only: this package records no session link, because a commit, ref move or rebase becomes a session link only through the change version that package 22 records for it; package 22's `SessionLinker` alone has a record operation (with packages 19, 22 and 49).
12. The rebase keeps each commit's author and sets the hub as committer. Without `expected_head_sha` the head read at the start of the request guards the compare-and-swap.
13. "Already based on `onto`" means `onto` is an ancestor of, or equal to, the branch head. "Every commit already contained in `onto`" means the replay produces no commit; the branch moves to `onto`.
14. The conflict report of a rebase carries `target_sha`, `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `commit_sha` and `files` with `path`, `kind`, `base`, `ours`, `theirs`; `landed_changes` and each `landed_by` are empty arrays and `change` is null, which §8.3.3 allows when unknown. Package 26 adds the attribution.
15. `parley scm commit` sends operations in command-line order across `--put`, `--delete` and `--move`, sends file content as `content_base64` with no `mode`, and sends a `change` object when any of `--change-target`, `--title`, `--intent`, `--draft` is given. A local file that cannot be read is a `usage_error` (exit 2) and no request is sent.
16. The PRD sets no time limit on writes and none is added; the read timeout of package 20 does not apply to write routes.
17. A path with a `.git` segment at any depth is refused, not only one that starts with `.git/`; git itself refuses such tree entries. A `chmod` takes `100644` or `100755` only: a mode change cannot turn a file into a symlink.
18. An org member has read access only (§3.3.6), so a member's write is refused by the route gate with `403 forbidden` and never reaches the push rules. The callers who reach rule 2 without the exemption are the owner's workspace-bound and path-scoped PATs, and every caller while `protect.owner_push` is false.
19. The hub's committer identity is the one `internal/gitrepo` uses for every commit the hub makes; this package adds no setting for it. When the admin token commits without an `author`, the author is that identity too, because the admin token has no user.
20. Every write goes through `Evaluate` and `Apply` of package 18 (decision 2 of that package). The version of a moved source branch is recorded by the ref-updated stage of package 22 inside `Apply`'s commit step, in one store transaction with the ref update (CHG-FR-010); this package passes the version kind, the session and the caller's credential and reads the recorded version from `Apply`'s result for the `change` member. Opening a change (`ChangeLinker`) happens after the ref has moved, as the mapping stage of package 19 does for a push. A stage error fails the request before the ref moves.
21. Revisions (`base_ref`, the `ref` of a ref creation, `onto`) are resolved with the resolver of package 20, in the four forms of §6.3: branch name, tag name, full ref name, commit id. `sha`, `expected_sha` and `expected_head_sha` are full 40-character ids.
22. The post-push listeners are notified by package 18, not here (with packages 18 and 37). Every write of this package reaches the ref writer with `via: "api"` and the request's session id, and the event step of `Apply` calls the registered post-push listeners with the slug, the accepted updates, that `via` and that session id. This package holds no listener registry and calls no listener, so the carry-patch triggers of package 37 reach API writes through package 18's one registration.
23. Ancestry and single-ref compare-and-swap are package 12's `IsAncestor` and `CompareAndSwapRef` in `internal/gitrepo` (with packages 12 and 18). This package declares neither again: the rebase asks `IsAncestor` whether `onto` is contained in the head, and every ref it moves goes through `Apply` of package 18.
24. Wiring is in `internal/hub/scm.go`: what this package has to be handed (the engine and ref writer of package 18, the event writer, the registration calls for `ChangeLinker` and `SessionLinker`) is composed there.
25. **Writes are counted through package 20's request recorder (with packages 20 and 51).** Each request that reaches a write route's handler is reported once to the request recorder of `internal/scm`, which package 20 declares and package 51 connects to `parley_scm_requests_total{op,result}`. The `op` values are `commit`, `ref_create`, `ref_move`, `ref_delete` and `rebase`. The `result` values are package 20's `ok` (a status below 400) and `error` (any other), plus the two that package 20's decision 23 leaves to writes: `ref_moved` for a `409 ref_moved` and `refused` for a `403` of a push rule. As with reads, a request refused by the shared checks or the write gate before the handler runs is not reported. This package declares no recorder of its own.

## Dependencies

- Package 20 scm_read_api (draft): the `internal/scm` route group, revision resolution, the ref and commit objects, the `[scm]` configuration section, `internal/gitrepo` including the trial rebase this package's rebase extends, and `internal/cli/scm.go`.
- Package 18 git_push_rules (draft): the rule engine that accepts or refuses a ref update and the ref writer with the compare-and-swap of refs, the ref-updated stages, the emission of `parley.git.push` and the call of the post-push listeners, both in `internal/gitserver/pushrule`, and the protected-branch test. Through it: package 12 workspace_sync_from_origin, which declares `IsAncestor` and `CompareAndSwapRef` in `internal/gitrepo`.
- Package 09 cli_foundation (draft) for the two commands and package 52 durable_event_log_and_stream (draft) for `parley.scm.commit`.
- Through interfaces, not dependencies: package 22 (`ChangeLinker`), package 49 (`SessionLinker`).
- The `git` command, 2.38 or later, at run time.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires.
- **Tracking branch**: In a fork, a branch that existed in the parent at fork time. It is read-only in the fork and always equals the parent's branch.
- **Protected branch**: A branch that moves only by landing a change, by sync from origin, or by a direct fast-forward push from the workspace's owner or the admin token. Nobody can force-push or delete it. By default the default branch.
- **Direct push**: A fast-forward update of a protected branch by the workspace's owner or the admin token, over git or the source control API, without a change. Allowed while the workspace setting `protect.owner_push` is true.
- **Change**: The unit of work: a proposal to add the commits of a source branch to a target branch, with a number, a title, an intent, versions and a state.
- **Version**: One head of a change's source branch. Every push, API commit or restack that moves the source creates a new version.
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Path-scoped token**: A PAT whose writes are limited to files matching a list of globs.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it).
- **Session**: An agent session: who ran, on which workspace, with what token usage, and which changes it produced.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Write-route gate

**Rationale:** A write must be refused before it reads or changes anything when the caller may not write or the workspace cannot take a write.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] IF a write route is called with a PAT that lacks the scope `git:write`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without reading the repository
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`; no ref moves and no event is emitted; the answer is the same whether or not the workspace exists
   Check: unit
   - setup: the write gate of internal/scm with a stub access component and a stub workspace lookup
   ```
   in internal/scm/write_test.go: wrap a probe handler in the write gate; send a request with a PAT whose scopes are {git:read}; assert status == 403 and error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert the probe handler did not run; the same request with scopes {git:write} runs the probe; an API key runs the probe
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF a write route is called by a caller whose access to the workspace is below write, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request without reading the repository
   → HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` when the caller has no access to the workspace; HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` when the caller has read access only; no ref moves
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/scm/write_test.go beside the scope test, a table over the access level the stub access component reports {none -> 404 not_found, read -> 403 forbidden, write -> probe runs, owner -> probe runs, admin -> probe runs}: assert status and error.error_type; assert the probe ran only in the last three rows
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF a write route is called by a caller with write access on a workspace that is not writable, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request by the workspace's status and leave the repository untouched
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_archived` for an archived workspace, `parent_archived` for a fork whose parent is archived, `workspace_busy` for a workspace (or a fork's parent) that is `pending`, `cloning` or in a reclone, archive or delete, and `workspace_not_ready` for a `failed` workspace
   Check: unit
   ```
   in internal/scm/write_test.go, a table over the workspace the stub lookup returns {status archived -> 409 workspace_archived; a fork with status ready whose parent is archived -> 409 parent_archived; pending -> 409 workspace_busy; cloning -> 409 workspace_busy; ready with an archive running -> 409 workspace_busy; a fork whose parent is cloning -> 409 workspace_busy; failed -> 409 workspace_not_ready; ready -> probe runs}: assert status and error.error_type; assert the probe ran only for ready
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] THE parleyd SHALL for any of the five write routes (`POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits`, `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs`, `PATCH /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name`, `DELETE /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name`, `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/rebase`), run the write gate before the route's own validation
   → each route answers the gate's refusal (`insufficient_scope`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `workspace_archived`, `parent_archived`, `workspace_busy`, `workspace_not_ready`) and never `invalid_request` when both apply
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
   - setup: the real router of internal/server with the scm routes registered
   ```

   ```

### REQ-2: Commit creation and its compare-and-swap

**Rationale:** An agent commits its edits in one request and is told when the branch moved under it, so it never overwrites work it has not seen (SCM-US-02).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` names an existing branch and an `expected_head_sha` equal to its head, THE parleyd SHALL create one commit whose parent is the branch head and whose tree is the parent's tree with the operations applied, and move the branch to it
   → HTTP 201 with `{commit, branch, change, change_error}`: `commit` is the commit object (40-character `sha`, `parents` holding exactly the old head), `branch` is the ref object at the new commit; `base_ref` is ignored
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
   - setup: an unprotected branch work at main's head
   - setup: the caller is the workspace owner with an API key
   ```
   in internal/scm/commit_test.go: head = rev-parse('work'); r = post('/workspaces/w/scm/commits', {branch:'work', expected_head_sha: head, message:'m', operations:[put a.txt 'hi']}); assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.commit.parents == [head]; assert r.json.commit.message == 'm'; assert r.json.branch.name == 'refs/heads/work' and r.json.branch.sha == r.json.commit.sha; assert len(r.json.commit.sha) == 40; assert git rev-parse refs/heads/work == r.json.commit.sha; assert git show work:a.txt == 'hi'; assert 'change' and 'change_error' are present and null; a second row sends base_ref:'nope' together with the right expected_head_sha and still gets 201
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] WHEN `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` names a branch that does not exist and a `base_ref` that resolves to a commit, THE parleyd SHALL create the commit on top of the commit `base_ref` resolves to and create the branch at the new commit
   → HTTP 201; `commit.parents` holds exactly the resolved base commit; the branch exists afterwards at `commit.sha`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
   ```
   in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table over base_ref {'main', 'refs/heads/main', the full id of main's head, a 7-character prefix of it}: r = post commits {branch:'new-<i>', base_ref, message, operations:[put x 'y']}; assert r.status == 201; assert r.json.commit.parents == [main head]; assert git rev-parse refs/heads/new-<i> == r.json.commit.sha
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any created commit, record the request's `author` name and e-mail as the author, or the caller's name and e-mail when `author` is absent, and the hub's identity as the committer
   → `commit.author` and `commit.committer` in the 201 answer, and the same values in the stored commit
   Check: unit
   - setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
   ```
   in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table {author {name:'A', email:'a@x'} given -> commit.author.name == 'A' and email == 'a@x'; author absent, caller user (Kim, kim@x) -> author is Kim; author absent, admin token -> author equals the hub identity}: in every row assert r.json.commit.committer.name and .email equal the hub's configured committer identity and git log -1 --format='%an|%ae|%cn|%ce' agrees with the response
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF the named branch exists and `expected_head_sha` is absent or differs from the branch head, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request, create no visible commit and leave the branch where it is
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `ref_moved` and `error.details.current_sha` equal to the branch's current head; no event is emitted
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
   - setup: a recording event sink

   in internal/scm/commit_test.go, a table over expected_head_sha for the existing branch work {absent, main's old parent id, 40 zeros}: r = post commits; assert r.status == 409; assert r.json.error.error_type == 'ref_moved'; assert r.json.error.details.current_sha == rev-parse(work); assert rev-parse(work) is unchanged; assert no event was recorded by the test event sink
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF the commit request is malformed: `branch` is missing or not a valid branch name, `message` is missing or empty, `operations` holds more than 1,000 entries, `author` lacks `name` or `email`, or the branch does not exist and `base_ref` is absent or resolves to no commit, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and move no ref
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`, except HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found` for a `base_ref` that resolves to no commit; exactly 1,000 operations are accepted
   Check: unit

   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] IF another write moves the branch between the read of its head and the compare-and-swap of a commit request, THEN THE parleyd SHALL answer the loser of the race as moved and leave only the winner's commit reachable from the branch

### REQ-3: File operations

**Rationale:** The four operations are the whole vocabulary a client has for describing an edit; each must do one predictable thing or fail the whole request.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a `put` operation carries a valid `path`, exactly one of `content` (UTF-8 text) and `content_base64`, and no `mode` or a `mode` of `100644`, `100755` or `120000`, THE parleyd SHALL create the file at `path`, or replace it, with the given bytes and mode, creating missing parent directories
   → the resulting tree holds the path as a blob with those bytes and that mode (`100644` when none is given); with mode `120000` the content is the link target
   Check: unit
   - setup: the operation applier of internal/gitrepo over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir() whose parent tree holds a.txt (100644), bin/run (100755), docs/guide.md and a submodule entry vendor/lib
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/treewrite_test.go, a table {put new/deep/f.txt content 'x' -> blob 'x' mode 100644; put a.txt content 'new' -> replaced, mode 100644; put img.bin content_base64 of bytes 00 ff 10 -> blob equals those bytes; put tool mode '100755' -> mode 100755; put link mode '120000' content 'a.txt' -> tree entry is a symlink whose target is 'a.txt'; put a.txt with its current content -> tree id equals the parent's tree id}: apply, then read back with git ls-tree -r and git cat-file blob
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a `delete`, `move` or `chmod` operation names an existing file (and, for `move`, a `to` that does not exist), THE parleyd SHALL remove the path for `delete`, rename `from` to `to` keeping content and mode for `move`, and change only the mode for `chmod`
   → the resulting tree lacks the deleted path; holds the moved file under `to` with the blob id and mode it had under `from`; holds the chmod-ed file with the same blob id and the new mode
   Check: unit
   - setup: the operation applier of internal/gitrepo over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir() whose parent tree holds a.txt (100644), bin/run (100755), docs/guide.md and a submodule entry vendor/lib
   ```
   in internal/gitrepo/treewrite_test.go, a table {delete a.txt -> a.txt absent; delete docs/guide.md -> docs/ absent from the tree (no empty directory); move bin/run -> tools/run: tools/run has the old blob id and mode 100755, bin/run absent; chmod a.txt 100755 -> same blob id, mode 100755}: apply and compare git ls-tree -r output with the expected entries
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE parleyd SHALL for any list of operations, apply them one at a time in request order, each to the tree the previous one left
   → `put a` followed by `delete a` leaves no `a`; a later operation may use a path an earlier one created or freed
   Check: unit
   - setup: the operation applier of internal/gitrepo over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir() whose parent tree holds a.txt (100644), bin/run (100755), docs/guide.md and a submodule entry vendor/lib

   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF an operation cannot apply to the tree as the earlier operations left it: `delete`, `move` or `chmod` of a missing path, `move` onto an existing path, `put` under a path that is a file, `put` onto a directory, or any operation on or under a submodule entry, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the whole request, naming the first operation that does not apply, and move no ref
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_operation` and `error.details.index` holding the zero-based index of that operation

1. [REQ-3.5] IF an operation is malformed: an unknown or missing `op`; a path that is empty, starts with `/`, has a `.` or `..` segment or a `.git` segment; a `put` with both or neither of `content` and `content_base64` or with invalid base64; a `put` mode outside `100644`, `100755`, `120000`; a `chmod` mode outside `100644`, `100755`; a missing field, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before resolving the parent

   Check: integration

### REQ-5: Push-rule refusals over the API

**Rationale:** The API and the git server are two doors to one repository; a write refused over git must be refused here too, with a machine-readable type per rule.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] THE parleyd SHALL for any ref update a write route is about to make, submit it to the push rule engine of package 18 (Evaluate in internal/gitserver/pushrule) with the caller facts, the full ref name, the `before` commit (none for a create) and the `after` commit (none for a delete), and make the update only when the engine accepts it, through the ref writer of the same package (Apply with via `api`)
   → one evaluation per request, made before the compare-and-swap; the commit named as `after` exists in the repository when the engine is called; the compare-and-swap, the workspace's `head_sha`, the ref-updated stages and `parley.git.push` are the ref writer's, and this package has no second writer
   Check: unit
   - setup: a ready workspace whose bare repository was made with git init in t.TempDir() and holds main with the files README.md, api/old.go and the directory docs/
   - setup: a fake rule engine that records each evaluation and accepts
   ```
   in internal/scm/rules_test.go, with a recording fake engine: a table {commit on existing branch -> (refs/heads/work, old, new); commit creating a branch -> (refs/heads/n, none, new); POST refs tag -> (refs/tags/v1, none, sha); PATCH ref -> (name, expected_sha, sha); DELETE ref -> (name, current, none); rebase -> (refs/heads/work, old, rebased head)}: assert exactly one engine call per request with those values and the request's credential; assert the call happened while rev-parse(ref) still returned the before value
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] IF the push rule engine refuses the ref update of a write, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request with the engine's message and the `error_type` of the refusing rule

**Rationale:** The owner exemption must behave the same at both doors, or the API becomes a way around (or a stricter copy of) branch protection.

   → HTTP 201; `parley.git.push` has `direct: true`; `change` and `change_error` are null; when the branch is the default branch the workspace's `head_sha` equals the new commit

[REQ-6.2] IF a commit on a protected branch comes from a caller or credential the owner exemption does not cover: the owner's workspace-bound PAT, the owner's path-scoped PAT, or any caller while `protect.owner_push` is false, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the commit and leave the protected branch where it is

   → HTTP 201 with the ref object; a bare `name` creates `refs/heads/<name>`; a tag is lightweight

[REQ-7.2] IF a ref creation request is invalid: `name` is missing, is not a valid git ref name, is `HEAD`, or lies outside `refs/heads/`, `refs/tags/` and `refs/parley/`; both or neither of `sha` and `ref` are given; `sha` is not a full 40-character id; the target resolves to no commit; or the ref already exists, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and create nothing
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for a bad name or target field; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found` for a target that resolves to no commit; HTTP 409 with `error_type` `ref_exists` for an existing ref; a name under `refs/parley/` answers HTTP 403 with `error_type` `hub_owned_ref`

   → HTTP 200 with the ref object at `sha`; a move to the commit the ref already has answers 200 and emits no event; a branch that is the source of a `draft` or `open` change gets a version of kind `ref`, recorded by the ref-updated stage of package 22 from the version kind this route passes to the ref writer

### REQ-8: Server-side rebase

**Rationale:** An agent keeps its branch current with the target without fetching, and gets a conflict as data when it cannot (SCM-US-05).

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/rebase` names a branch that has commits not in `onto`, where `onto` is not an ancestor of the branch head, and the replay applies without conflict, THE parleyd SHALL replay those commits in order on top of the commit `onto` resolves to, keeping each commit's author and message and setting the hub as committer, move the branch to the result by compare-and-swap and emit one `parley.git.push` event
   → HTTP 200 with `{status: "rebased", branch, old_head_sha, new_head_sha, onto_sha, change}`; `branch` is the ref object at `new_head_sha`; the event has `forced: true` when the old head is not an ancestor of the new one
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1)
   - setup: a recording event sink
   ```
   in internal/scm/rebase_test.go: r = post('/workspaces/w/scm/rebase', {branch:'topic', onto:'main', expected_head_sha: T2}); assert 200; assert r.json.status == 'rebased'; old_head_sha == T2; onto_sha == M2; new_head_sha == rev-parse(topic) != T2; branch.sha == new_head_sha; change == null; assert git rev-list --count main..topic == 2 and merge-base(main, topic) == M2; assert the two new commits keep the authors and messages of T1 and T2 and have the hub as committer; assert git diff T1^ T1 equals the diff of the first new commit; assert one push event {before: T2, after: new, forced: true, via:'api'}; a second row without expected_head_sha -> 200
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN a rebase request names an `onto` that is an ancestor of the branch head or equal to it, THE parleyd SHALL answer without moving the branch and without emitting an event
   → HTTP 200 with `status` `up_to_date` and `new_head_sha` equal to `old_head_sha`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1)
   - setup: a recording event sink
   ```
   in internal/scm/rebase_test.go, a table over onto {M1 (an ancestor of topic), T2 (the head itself), 'topic'}: assert 200, status == 'up_to_date', old_head_sha == new_head_sha == T2, onto_sha == the resolved commit; assert rev-parse(topic) == T2 and the sink is empty and the rule engine was not called
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN a rebase request names a branch whose every commit is already contained in `onto`, by ancestry or because each replayed commit changes nothing, THE parleyd SHALL move the branch to the `onto` commit
   → HTTP 200 with `status` `rebased` and `new_head_sha` equal to `onto_sha`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1)
   - setup: a recording event sink
   ```
   in internal/scm/rebase_test.go, a table {branch behind at M1, onto main -> new_head_sha == M2, event forced false; branch whose two commits were cherry-picked onto main as M3, M4, onto main -> new_head_sha == M4, event forced true}: assert 200 and status == 'rebased'; assert rev-parse(branch) == rev-parse(main)
   ```
1. [REQ-8.4] IF a commit of the branch does not apply on top of `onto`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL abandon the rebase, leave the branch at its old head and report the conflict
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `rebase_conflict` and `error.details` holding the conflict report, the type ConflictReport of internal/gitrepo that package 20 declares (`target_sha`, `head_sha`, `base_sha`, `commit_sha`, `files` with `path`, `kind`, `base`, `ours`, `theirs`, `landed_by`; `landed_changes`; `change`); no ref moves, no event is emitted and no temporary file of the rebase remains
   Check: integration
   - setup: a ready workspace whose repository holds main (commits M1, M2) and the unprotected branch topic (commits T1, T2 on top of M1), with a conflicting edit of a.txt on both sides
   - setup: a recording event sink

   ```
1. [REQ-8.5] IF a rebase request is invalid: `branch` or `onto` is missing, `branch` is not an existing branch, `onto` resolves to no commit, or the commits to replay include a merge commit, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the rebase and move nothing
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `merge_commits_unsupported` for a merge commit in the range; HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for a missing field or a `branch` that is not under `refs/heads/`; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found` for an unknown branch or `onto`

### REQ-9: CLI commands for commit and rebase

**Rationale:** A person or a script commits local files and rebases a branch from a shell with one command each.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-9.1] WHEN `parley scm commit <slug>` runs with `--branch`, `--message`, `--expected-head` and any number of `--put <repo-path>=<local-file>`, `--delete <repo-path>` and `--move <from>=<to>` flags, THE parley CLI SHALL send one `POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits` whose `operations` follow command-line order, with each `--put` file's bytes as `content_base64`, and print the hub's answer

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: An agent commits edits to its fork without a clone and is told when the branch moved

1. **agent** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/<fork>/scm/commits with a fork-bound PAT, branch greeting, base_ref main, a message and three operations (two puts and a delete)
2. **parleyd** passes the write gate, validates the body, resolves main in the fork and applies the operations to its tree
3. **parleyd** creates the commit, has the push rule engine accept the creation of refs/heads/greeting and creates the branch by compare-and-swap
4. **parleyd** emits parley.git.push (created, via api) and parley.scm.commit and answers 201 with the commit and the branch
5. **agent** reads GET /api/v1/workspaces/<fork>/scm/file?ref=greeting&path=api/greeting.go and receives the bytes it put
6. **git client** fetches the fork over /git and sees refs/heads/greeting at the commit the API answered
7. **agent** posts a second commit to greeting with expected_head_sha set to main's head
8. **parleyd** answers 409 ref_moved with details.current_sha equal to the first commit and leaves greeting where it is

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the parleyd HTTP server and its check pipeline, the write gate and commit handler of internal/scm, internal/gitrepo running the git binary on a bare repository, the push rule engine of package 18, the event log, the read routes of package 20, the git smart HTTP server

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 by the Run function of internal/hub with a real store and a data directory in t.TempDir()
- a registered workspace cloned from a local origin repository made with git init, and a task fork of it with a fork-bound PAT holding git:read and git:write

**End state:**

- refs/heads/greeting exists in the fork at the commit the first answer named, with one parent equal to main's head
- the file route returns the put content at ref greeting
- a stock git ls-remote of the fork lists refs/heads/greeting at that commit
- the event log holds one parley.git.push with via api and created true and one parley.scm.commit for the branch, and none for the refused second request
- the second request was answered 409 ref_moved with the first commit as current_sha

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/scm_write_test.go: r = POST commits {branch:'greeting', base_ref:'main', message, operations:[put api/greeting.go, put docs/g.md, delete api/old.go]}; assert r.status == 201; sha = r.json.commit.sha; assert GET file(ref greeting, api/greeting.go).body == content; assert exec('git ls-remote <hub>/git/<org>/<fork>.git refs/heads/greeting') starts with sha; r2 = POST commits {branch:'greeting', expected_head_sha: mainHead, ...}; assert r2.status == 409 and r2.json.error.details.current_sha == sha; assert GET /events/log filtered to the fork lists parley.git.push then parley.scm.commit once each
```

### PATH-2: A developer commits a local file and rebases the branch from the shell

1. **developer** runs parley scm commit <slug> --branch topic --base main --message 'Add notes' --put notes.md=./notes.md
2. **parley CLI** reads GET …/scm/refs/topic, receives 404 ref_not_found, and sends POST …/scm/commits with base_ref main and the file as content_base64
3. **parleyd** creates the commit and the branch topic and answers 201
4. **parley CLI** prints the answer on stdout and exits 0
5. **developer** after another commit reached main, runs parley scm rebase <slug> topic --onto main
6. **parley CLI** sends POST …/scm/rebase with branch topic and onto main
7. **parleyd** replays the commit of topic onto main's head, has the push rule engine accept the non-fast-forward move, moves topic by compare-and-swap and emits parley.git.push with forced true
8. **parley CLI** prints the answer with status rebased and exits 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the parley CLI root command and its HTTP client, the parleyd HTTP server, the commit, ref and rebase handlers of internal/scm, internal/gitrepo running the git binary, the push rule engine of package 18, the event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 by the Run function of internal/hub with a real store and a data directory in t.TempDir()
- a registered workspace owned by the developer, whose API key is in PARLEY_API_KEY
- a local file notes.md in t.TempDir()
- main is not protected in this workspace (protected_branches set to an empty list) so a second commit can be put on main through the API

**End state:**

- topic holds exactly one commit ahead of main and its parent is main's current head
- notes.md at ref topic has the local file's bytes
- the first command printed a document with commit and branch; the second printed status rebased with old_head_sha different from new_head_sha
- both commands exited 0
- the event log holds a parley.git.push for topic with forced true and via api

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/scm_write_test.go: out1, code1 = runCLI('scm','commit',slug,'--branch','topic','--base','main','--message','Add notes','--put','notes.md='+local); assert code1 == 0 and json(out1).branch.name == 'refs/heads/topic'; POST commits on main (other file) with the owner key; out2, code2 = runCLI('scm','rebase',slug,'topic','--onto','main'); assert code2 == 0; j = json(out2); assert j.status == 'rebased' and j.onto_sha == main head and j.new_head_sha != j.old_head_sha; assert GET compare(base main, head topic).ahead == 1 and .behind == 0; assert GET file(topic, notes.md) == local bytes
```

### PATH-3: The owner pushes directly to a protected branch through the API and other credentials cannot

1. **developer** as the workspace's owner, sends POST …/scm/commits with an API key, branch main and main's head as expected_head_sha
2. **parleyd** builds the commit and submits the fast-forward update of the protected branch to the push rule engine, which accepts it under the owner exemption
3. **parleyd** moves main, updates the workspace's head_sha, emits parley.git.push with direct true, opens no change and answers 201 with change null
4. **agent** sends the same kind of request to main with the owner's workspace-bound PAT and the new head as expected_head_sha
5. **parleyd** answers 403 protected_branch with the rule's message and leaves main where the owner put it
6. **org member** sends a commit request for main with an API key
7. **parleyd** answers 403 forbidden at the write gate, because a member has read access only, and moves nothing

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the parleyd HTTP server and its check pipeline, the workspace access rule, the commit and ref handlers of internal/scm, the push rule engine of package 18 with the owner exemption, internal/gitrepo running the git binary, the event log

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 by the Run function of internal/hub with a real store and a data directory in t.TempDir()
- a registered workspace in an organization, with default settings (main protected, protect.owner_push true)
- its owner's API key, a PAT of the owner bound to the workspace with git:write, and the API key of a second user who is a member of the organization

**End state:**

- main is at the owner's commit and the workspace record's head_sha equals it
- the event log holds exactly one parley.git.push for refs/heads/main, with direct true and via api
- no change exists whose source is main
- the bound PAT's commit request was answered 403 with error_type protected_branch and the member's was answered 403 with error_type forbidden
- refs/heads/main still exists

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/scm_write_test.go: r = POST commits as owner {branch:'main', expected_head_sha: head, message, operations:[put CHANGELOG.md]}; assert r.status == 201 and r.json.change == null; assert GET /workspaces/<slug>.head_sha == r.json.commit.sha; ev = events of type parley.git.push for refs/heads/main; assert len(ev) == 1 and ev[0].metadata.direct == true; r2 = POST commits with the owner's bound PAT and expected_head_sha == r.json.commit.sha; assert r2.status == 403 and r2.json.error.error_type == 'protected_branch'; r3 = the same request with the member's API key; assert r3.status == 403 and r3.json.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; assert GET /scm/refs/main .sha == r.json.commit.sha
```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/scm/... ./internal/gitrepo/... ./internal/cli/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `09` — builds its CLI commands on the client, output and exit-code helpers of the CLI foundation
- `18` — the push rule engine (Evaluate) and the ref writer (Apply with via api) in internal/gitserver/pushrule that every API write goes through: the owner exemption, the compare-and-swap of refs, the ref-updated stages and the parley.git.push emission
- `20` — the internal/scm route group, revision resolution, the ref and commit objects, the [scm] configuration section, internal/gitrepo with the trial rebase, and the scm command group of the CLI
- `52` — emits its hub events through the event log component

## Tasks

### 1. Gate every write route by scope, access and workspace status (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.1, REQ-1.2, REQ-1.3

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the gate's behaviours to internal/scm/write_test.go as table-driven tests around a probe handler, with a stub access component and a stub workspace lookup, and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Add the write gate in internal/scm/write.go as a wrapper for a route handler: it declares the PAT scope git:write and the workspace need write through the check positions of internal/server, so the conventions' order holds (scope before access, access before validation)
- 1.3 After access passes, load the workspace and refuse by status: archived answers 409 workspace_archived; a fork whose parent is archived answers 409 parent_archived; pending, cloning or a running reclone, archive or delete (on the workspace or, for a fork, on its parent) answers 409 workspace_busy; failed answers 409 workspace_not_ready
- 1.4 Hand the wrapped handler the caller, the credential and the loaded workspace so that no write handler looks them up a second time
- 1.5 Use the error constructors of internal/server for every refusal; add parent_archived, workspace_busy and workspace_not_ready through the constructor for specific types only where the workspace package does not already export them

**Touches:**

- `internal/scm/write.go`
- `internal/scm/write_test.go`

**Done when:**

- the checks of the criteria listed above exist as tests, are executable and pass
- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 2. Create, move and delete branches and tags by compare-and-swap (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the ref behaviours to internal/scm/refs_write_test.go against a bare repository made with git init in t.TempDir(), a recording event sink, a recording ref-updated stage and a fake change linker, and confirm they fail
- 2.2 Declare the interface ChangeLinker in internal/scm/linker.go with a registration function RegisterChangeLinker and three operations: find the draft or open change whose source is a branch (with its current version); check an opening before a branch moves; open a change after a branch moved. The default reports no change for any branch and refuses a check; package 22 registers the real one. Recording a version is not an operation of the linker: package 22 does it in the ref-updated stage it registers with the ref writer of package 18
- 2.3 Add the shared ref update step in internal/scm/refupdate.go, used by every write route: take the full ref name, the before commit (none for a create), the after commit (none for a delete), the version kind of the route (commit, ref, rebase or none) and the session; call Evaluate of internal/gitserver/pushrule with the caller facts (level, credential kind and id, user, binding, paths) and, on acceptance, Apply of the same package with via api and the version kind, then its event step; Apply makes the compare-and-swap, sets head_sha, runs the ref-updated stages in its commit step, reports fork activity and emits parley.git.push with created, deleted, forced and direct, and its event step calls the post-push listeners of package 18 with the slug, the accepted updates, via api and the session, so this package writes no ref and no push event and notifies no listener itself; return the engine's direct flag and the version the ref writer reports for the update
- 2.4 Map the ref writer's outcome ref_moved to 409 ref_moved with details.current_sha read after the failure; pass an error a ref-updated stage returned through with its status and error_type, and answer 500 internal for one that carries none
- 2.5 Report every write request that reaches a write route's handler exactly once to the request recorder of package 20 (the recorder interface of internal/scm that feeds parley_scm_requests_total{op,result}; declare no second recorder): op is commit for POST …/scm/commits, ref_create for POST …/scm/refs, ref_move for PATCH …/scm/refs/*name, ref_delete for DELETE …/scm/refs/*name and rebase for POST …/scm/rebase; result is ok for a status below 400 and error otherwise, as package 20 defines them, except ref_moved for a 409 ref_moved and refused for a 403 of a push rule; a request the write gate refused is not reported
- 2.6 Register POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs behind the write gate: a bare name is a branch; accept only refs/heads/ and refs/tags/ names that git check-ref-format accepts (add this ref-name check to internal/gitrepo; package 19 reuses it), pass refs/parley/ names on to the rule engine, and refuse every other namespace and HEAD with 400 invalid_request; require exactly one of sha (a full 40-character id) and ref (a revision in the four forms of §6.3, resolved with the resolver of package 20); the target must resolve to a commit, else 404 ref_not_found; an existing ref answers 409 ref_exists; answer 201 with the ref object of package 20
- 2.7 Register PATCH /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name: resolve the name as a full ref name or a branch name; require sha and expected_sha as full ids; a sha that is no commit answers 404 ref_not_found; a sha equal to the current commit answers 200 without an update or an event; otherwise run the shared update step with version kind ref, so that the stage of package 22 records the version when the branch is the source of a draft or open change
- 2.8 Register DELETE /workspaces/:slug/scm/refs/*name with the optional query parameter expected_sha: a branch that the linker reports as the source of a draft or open change answers 409 ref_in_use; otherwise run the shared update step with the current commit (or expected_sha) as before and version kind none and answer 204 with no body
- 2.9 Leave the deleted ref's commits in the repository: no object is pruned by a delete

**Touches:**

- `internal/scm/linker.go`
- `internal/scm/refupdate.go`
- `internal/scm/refs_write.go`
- `internal/scm/refs_write_test.go`
- `internal/gitrepo`

**Done when:**

- `go test ./... -count=1` passes
- `golangci-lint run ./...` passes

### 3. Apply file operations to a tree without a working copy (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, REQ-3.3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Add the operation behaviours to internal/gitrepo/treewrite_test.go as tables over a repository made with git init in t.TempDir() that also holds an executable file, a nested directory and a submodule entry, and confirm they fail
- 3.2 Add the operation applier in internal/gitrepo/treewrite.go: given a parent commit and an ordered list of operations it returns the id of the resulting tree, or an error value carrying the zero-based index of the first operation that cannot apply
- 3.3 Work in a temporary index file private to the call (never the repository's own index, never a working tree): load the parent's tree, then apply each operation to the index as the previous one left it
- 3.4 put: write the bytes as a blob and set the entry with the given mode (100644 when none); a mode of 120000 stores the content as the link target
- 3.5 delete: remove the entry; move: re-add the entry's blob id and mode under the new path and remove the old one; chmod: keep the blob id and set the mode
- 3.6 Report as not applicable, with the operation's index: delete, move or chmod of a path that is not a file in the index; move onto an existing file or directory; put where an ancestor of the path is a file; put onto a directory; any operation on or under an entry of mode 160000
- 3.7 Write the tree from the index and remove the temporary index file on every exit, success or failure
- 3.8 Add commit creation from a tree beside it: parents, message, author name and e-mail, committer identity and both times are parameters; nothing is read from the environment or the user's git configuration

**Touches:**

- `internal/gitrepo/treewrite.go`
- `internal/gitrepo/treewrite_test.go`

### 4. Create a commit from file operations and move one branch (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2, REQ-3.4, REQ-3.5, REQ-3.6, REQ-3.7

**Steps:**

- 4.1 Add the commit behaviours to internal/scm/commit_test.go and the configuration behaviour to internal/config/config_test.go and confirm they fail
- 4.2 Add the key max_commit_size to the [scm] section of internal/config: a size, default 32MB; register POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/commits behind the write gate with that value as the route's own body limit in place of [server].max_body_size
- 4.3 Validate the body before touching the repository and answer 400 invalid_request for: a missing or invalid branch name, a missing or empty message, an author without name or email, more than 1,000 operations, and any malformed operation (unknown op, a path that is empty, starts with /, or has a ., .. or .git segment, both or neither of content and content_base64, invalid base64, a put mode outside 100644, 100755 and 120000, a chmod mode outside 100644 and 100755, a missing field)
- 4.4 Resolve the parent: for an existing branch the parent is its head, base_ref is ignored, and an expected_head_sha that is absent or different answers 409 ref_moved with details.current_sha; for a missing branch base_ref is required (400 invalid_request) and must resolve to a commit (404 ref_not_found) through the revision resolver of package 20
- 4.5 Apply the operations with the applier of internal/gitrepo; an operation that cannot apply answers 400 invalid_operation with details.index
- 4.6 Refuse a tree equal to the parent's tree with 400 empty_commit unless allow_empty is true; operations may be empty or absent
- 4.7 Create the commit: the request's author or else the caller's name and e-mail (the hub's identity for the admin token), the hub's identity as committer, the current time for both
- 4.8 Move or create the branch through the shared ref update step with the parent as before (none for a new branch) and version kind commit; a lost compare-and-swap answers 409 ref_moved and the unreferenced commit is left for git's garbage collection
- 4.9 Answer 201 with commit (the commit object of package 20, with stats), branch (the ref object), and change and change_error both null; the task that adds the commit's consequences fills them

### 5. Rebase a branch on the server (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-8, REQ-1.4

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the rebase behaviours to internal/scm/rebase_test.go and the five-route gate table to internal/scm/write_routes_test.go and confirm they fail
- 5.2 Register POST /workspaces/:slug/scm/rebase behind the write gate; require branch (an existing branch, by bare or full name) and onto (a revision in the four forms of §6.3, resolved with the resolver of package 20); an optional expected_head_sha must be a full id and must equal the head, else 409 ref_moved with details.current_sha
- 5.3 Answer 200 with status up_to_date, equal old and new head, and no update when onto is an ancestor of the head or equal to it, asked with IsAncestor of internal/gitrepo (package 12, not declared again here)
- 5.4 Refuse with 400 merge_commits_unsupported when any commit of the branch that is not in onto has more than one parent
- 5.5 Replay the commits oldest first onto the onto commit with the rebase of internal/gitrepo that package 20's comparison uses for its trial, extended to keep the result: each new commit keeps its author and message and takes the hub as committer; a commit that changes nothing on its new base is skipped; when nothing is left the result is the onto commit
- 5.6 On the first commit that does not apply, stop, remove every temporary file of the replay and answer 409 rebase_conflict with details holding the ConflictReport of internal/gitrepo that package 20 declares (no second report type): target_sha, head_sha, base_sha (the merge base), commit_sha and one files entry per conflicted path with its kind and its base, ours and theirs entries; landed_by and landed_changes are empty arrays and change is null
- 5.7 Move the branch through the shared ref update step with the head read at the start as before and version kind rebase, so a branch that moved meanwhile answers 409 ref_moved

### 8. Give an API commit the consequences of a push (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4

**Steps:**

- 8.1 Add the consequence behaviours to internal/scm/commit_events_test.go and internal/scm/session_test.go with a recording event sink, a recording ref-updated stage, a fake change linker, a fake session linker and the real idempotency helper of internal/server, and confirm they fail
- 8.2 After a commit's branch has moved, emit parley.scm.commit after parley.git.push, with metadata branch (the short name), sha, parent_sha and files: the paths the commit changed against its parent, both paths of a move, sorted, cut to 100
- 8.3 Declare the interface SessionLinker in internal/scm/session.go (caller, session id, workspace -> accepted, refused, or internal error) with a registration call, the same name and check packages 19 and 22 declare in their own Go packages; package 49 owns the check and hands it to all three. The interface is check-only here: the session link is recorded by package 22 with the change version, never by this package. On the commit and rebase routes check a given session_id after body validation and before the parent is resolved; a refusal, or no registered linker, answers 400 unknown_session
- 8.4 Carry an accepted session_id onto the emitted events, the commit object's session_id, the ref writer (which hands it to the ref-updated stages) and every linker call
- 8.5 Leave the post-push listeners to package 18: its ref writer calls them from the event step with via api and the session id this package passed; add no listener registry and no listener call to internal/scm, and compose what this package is handed in internal/hub/scm.go
- 8.6 When the ref writer reports a version for the moved branch (the source of a draft or open change), answer change {workspace_slug, number, version} from it
- 8.7 With a change object in the request (on an unprotected branch): ask the linker to check the opening after the push rules accepted and before the compare-and-swap, and pass its error through unchanged (403 insufficient_scope, the 400 and 409 of the opening checks); with no linker registered answer 400 invalid_request; after the branch moved, open the change and answer it with version 1
- 8.8 Without a change object, in a fork whose auto_change is true, when the branch is the fork's own and has no draft or open change: ask the linker to open a change in the parent with the fork's base branch as target; on failure keep the commit and answer change null with change_error {error_type, message}
- 8.9 Wrap the three POST routes (commits, refs, rebase) in the idempotency helper of internal/server so that a replay answers 200 with the recorded body, a different body under the same key answers 409 conflict, and refused requests are not recorded
